dedupe_keys.name: physics based data generation engine simulating transmission power system performance during hurricanes texas university of florida and university of utah

description: This Zenodo record by Xiao Zhu and Ge Ou of the University of Florida with Fatemehalsadat Jafarishiadeh, Xin Li, Mostafa Ardakani and Zhaoxia Pu of the University of Utah provides a data generation engine that simulates the performance of transmission power infrastructure during hurricanes. The page explains that wind and flood loads beyond design limits damage towers, poles and substations, changing network topology and causing outages, and that resilience research lacks realistic infrastructure and system data; the engine is built to fill that gap. The files include Python scripts for the main run, infrastructure failure calculation and hurricane security-constrained unit commitment, wind speed and angle fields at 1, 2 and 4 km in MATLAB format, a transmission line fragility table, an infrastructure GIS table, a 2K system workbook, a Texas boundary and base map, a load factor file and installation notes. It is free under CC BY 4.0, first published in October 2022. Coverage is Texas. Caveats: the page gives no documentation of fields or validation beyond the files, and it has not been updated. Simulation uses are hurricane wind fragility of transmission lines feeding dispatch and outage studies. Related records: data-odin-real-time-outages-county gives observed US outage data for comparison.
